rows.note: Use this as the standard term for the perceived frequency of a musical or other sound.

example.english: The pitch of this song keeps rising and falling, and it sounds uncomfortable.
example.traditional: 呢首歌個音高忽高忽低，聽落好唔舒服。
example.jyutping: ne1 sau2 go1 go3 jam1 gou1 fat1 gou1 fat1 dai1 teng1 lok6 hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6

rows.note: Use this for presenting an idea, product, or proposal persuasively in an attempt to gain support or make a sale.

example.english: We need to pitch this new proposal to clients today.
example.traditional: 我哋今日要向客戶推銷呢個新方案。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 jat6 jiu3 hoeng3 haak3 wu6 teoi1 siu1 ni1 go3 san1 fong1 on3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for physically throwing something, including throwing something away.

example.english: Don't pitch the ball around carelessly; someone could get hurt.
example.traditional: 唔好亂咁掟個波，會整親人㗎。
example.jyutping: m4 hou2 lyun6 gam3 deng3 go3 bo1 wui5 zing2 can1 jan4 gaa3

rows.note: Use this for the playing field in a football, rugby, cricket, or similar sports context.

example.english: The pitch is completely soaked, so the match has to be postponed.
example.jyutping: kau4 coeng4 sap1 saai3 coeng4 bo1 jiu3 jin4 kei4

rows.note: Use this for persuasive sales talk or a presentation intended to sell something.

example.english: His pitch was so persuasive that I almost bought a new vacuum cleaner.
example.traditional: 佢嗰套推銷話術好有說服力，搞到我差啲買咗部新吸塵機。
example.jyutping: keoi5 go2 tou3 teoi1 siu1 waa6 seot6 hou2 jau5 seoi3 fuk6 lik6 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 caa1 di1 maai5 zo2 bou6 san1 kap1 can4 gei1

rows.note: Use this specifically when putting up or erecting a tent.

example.english: We'll pitch a tent in the countryside and sleep under the stars tonight.
example.traditional: 我哋去郊外搭帳篷，今晚喺星光底下瞓。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 heoi3 gaau1 ngoi6 daap3 zoeng3 pung4 gam1 maan1 hai2 sing1 gwong1 dai2 haa6 fan3
